implementation_notes: C has no garbage collector, no immutable data structures and no closure capture, so the snapshot half of STM is pure copying - which is exactly the half that must be cheap. The only workable realisation is a version-stamped cell plus a hand-written read set: each shared struct carries an `unsigned long version`, the transaction records (pointer, observed version, old value) for everything it reads, and the body returns a write list that commit validates and then installs under a short lock held only for the swap. Note what this becomes: a coarse critical section at commit. That is defensible for short, low-contention operations and indefensible for anything else, because the commit lock serialises every transaction that writes. Prefer one of the three honest alternatives for C: a coarse-grained mutex around the whole operation when the critical section is provably short; per-field atomics with a compare-and-swap retry loop when exactly one field changes; or thread confinement with message passing when you control the architecture. C++11's std::atomic and C11's std::atomic give the primitive; nothing above it is in the standard library.
alternative: pthread_mutex_t around the composite operation (Coarse-Grained Lock) for short critical sections, or C11 std::atomic compare_exchange with a retry loop for single-location updates
pitfalls: The two CAS operations are not atomic together: if the first succeeds and the second fails, the debit is already visible and only a compensating write repairs it - that is compensation logic, the anti-pattern STM removes.
Structs are copied by value into the read set, so a snapshot of a large struct is a large memcpy; keep transactional state small or hold a pointer to an immutable node.
memory_order_relaxed gives atomicity but no happens-before edge, so a concurrent reader can observe a torn logical relationship between two atomics.
There is no way to intercept a plain assignment, so a missed access is silently outside the read set - unlike a language where the transaction macro sees every ref operation.
Live-lock: without randomised backoff two threads can livelock forever.
